title: Rework claims server-side fixes but the diff contains no server or shared hunks
evidence:
The accumulator now carries a latched `restarted` flag: only the FIRST batch
  strictly after `corrected_at` resets to 0, later batches continue the
  fresh cycle.
- W2: the legacy terminal fallback skips `updated_at` when the row was
  taken over (the takeover bumps it post-terminal; the terminal entry is
  omitted rather than faked at the takeover instant).
- W7/W8: OQ-5 toast pinned at const + firing arm; terminalized_at
  integration pins for all five writers.
detail: The rework commit's headline fixes (B1 latched restart flag, W2 legacy terminal fallback, W8 terminalized_at integration pins) are server-side, but the diff's file list is client/spec/YAML only. Claims undelivered or unverifiable.
recommended_fix: Include the builder/sweep/SQL/test hunks in the review diff, or narrow the commit message and rework notes to what the commit actually changes.

evidence:
import shared/notification.{
  type Notification, AiComplete, BatchComplete, NewApplication, PaymentConfirmed,
-  VacancyClosed, VacancyClosing, VacancyExtended,
+  ReferenceAwaitingCorrection, ReferenceCompleted, ReferenceDeclined,

+  VacancyExtended,
}
...
+      reference_call.AttemptLogEntry(
+        kind: "",
...
+    attempt_log: [],
detail: The dropdown imports five Reference* NotificationType variants and reference_panel constructs reference_call.AttemptLogEntry and reads call.attempt_log, but no shared/notification.gleam or shared/reference_call.gleam hunk exists in the diff. As-diffed, the tree cannot compile.
recommended_fix: Confirm the shared codec and record hunks are in the commit; if they are truly absent, the build is red and the diff is incomplete.

title: Send-batch merge ignores kind despite the adjacent comment claiming kind is checked
detail: The merge condition checks send-ness twice plus equal `at` — never `entry.kind == first_kind(batch)`. Two cadence steps sharing one sweep timestamp (e.g. co_nudge + reminder) collapse into one line labeled by the first kind; the later event vanishes from timeline and export.
recommended_fix: Add kind equality to the merge condition so only same-kind same-at entries batch together; separate batches per kind per timestamp.

title: Timeline/export consistency test asserts weak proxies, not table agreement
detail: For six of eight statuses the test only checks non-empty and not-'In progress'. Mismatched pairs (e.g. unreachable's timeline 'Closed — no reply' vs export 'Couldn't be reached') are never compared; a swapped label pair would pass.
recommended_fix: Pin the exact (status -> label) pair for every terminal status in both tables, or rename the test to what it actually asserts.

title: Dropdown reference-types test never exercises the decode path the story exists to fix
detail: The test constructs the five variants directly and only asserts the title renders. The AC5 decode half — a reference_* row decoding through type_decoder without failing the whole list — is never exercised anywhere in this diff.
recommended_fix: Add a shared round-trip test through type_decoder for all five variants, and a dropdown test decoding a fixture list containing reference_* rows.

title: Generated export text carries em-dash joins the W5 scan does not pin
evidence:
TimelineLine(label <> " — " <> channels, first_at(entries))
...
      attempt.at
      <> " - "
      <> attempt.channel
      <> " - "
      <> attempt.outcome
detail: The old export used hyphen separators; the new export embeds the timeline labels' runtime em-dash join ("Invitation sent — email + SMS"). The W5 scan covers consts and fn-built labels only, so this generated landlord-facing text is unpinned against the em-dash ban.
recommended_fix: Either use hyphen separators in generated export text or extend the scan to pin the runtime join string.
